chapter_theme: The worthy recipient (பாத்திரம்): a gift as small as a sesame seed to a knower of Siva yields release, powers and the highest joy, while gold as vast as the earth given to fools bears no fruit. The other verses describe those who know the Lord, and only loosely fit the title.

501.reading: Gold the size of a sesame seed given to a knower of Siva yields its fruit: release, siddhi and the highest enjoyment; gold the size of the earth given to fools loses its fruit, and the highest enjoyment fails.
501.nuance: The contrast is between திலம் (sesame) and நிலம் (earth), one letter apart. The worth of the gift lies in the recipient's knowledge, not in its size or the recipient's need.

502.reading: Some went and came to know the Lord who masters Death, who eats the lives of those who stand and watch, who has the power to take life, and who gives grace to those who understand rightly; they became even gods.
502.nuance: The first two lines are ambiguous: காலனை and குணத்தனை may describe Death or the Lord who subdued him. Placed in this chapter, these knowers are presumably the worthy recipients.

503.reading: I have not let go of him since I was an embryo, have not left the truth, and seek the feet of the Changeless; putting away falsehood, I seek the feet of the one with plaited matted hair, and become like a lamp that needs no ghee.
503.nuance: விகிர்தன் is an epithet of Siva. The last line, நெய்விட்டிலாத இடிஞ்சில், is obscure: a lamp burning without ghee (an inner light) or an empty lamp; the reading is a guess.

504.reading: What is to become becomes, what is to perish perishes, what is to go goes and what is to come comes; the guardian named Nandi showed this and saw it, and the young kin does as he is bidden.
504.nuance: The repetitions in lines 1 and 2 state that things take their course. இளங்கிளையோன் (the young kin) may be the disciple or the poet himself; காட்டித்துக் looks corrupt.

links.note: Both say a small gift in worthy hands grows beyond its size: the Naladiyar's banyan seed shades the sky, Tirumular's sesame of gold yields release and siddhi.

Both say which gift truly counts. The Kural makes the recipient's need the test, calling all other giving a measured loan; Tirumular makes it the recipient's knowledge of Siva, and says gifts to fools bear no fruit however large. The conflict depends on taking மூடர் as the spiritually ignorant whatever their need.
505 continues the point from the other side: a gift to those without conduct or vows is like milking a barren cow or a crop past its season.

Kural 269 says 'கூற்றம் குதித்தலும் கைகூடும்', even leaping over Death becomes possible for those who have the strength of tapas. Tirumanthiram 502 says some went and came to know the Lord who masters Death ('காலனை'), and 'தேவருமாமே', became even gods. The Kural gives the escape from Death to tapas; the Tirumanthiram gives it to knowing the Lord who is Death's master.

Tirumanthiram 504 says 'ஆவன ஆவ அழிவ அழிவன, போவன போவ புகுவ புகுவன', what is to become becomes and what is to go goes, as Nandi showed. Kural 376 says what is not one's own will not stay however one cherishes it, and what is one's own will not go however one throws it away. Both state that what is allotted comes and goes regardless of effort; the Tirumanthiram makes it the teaching of the guru, which the disciple then follows.

source_issues: 501: the line division is broken; தரும் belongs to the end of line 2 (பரபோகமும் தரும்) but is printed at the start of line 3.
